title: CBSE Class 12 Business Studies · Practice paper 2
subject: Business Studies
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 34 questions. All questions are compulsory.
Marks are indicated against each question.
Answers should be brief and to the point.
Answers to the questions carrying 3 marks may be from 50 to 75 words.
Answers to the questions carrying 4 marks may be about 150 words.
Answers to the questions carrying 6 marks may be about 200 words.
Attempt all parts of the questions together.

The board paper numbers the questions 1 to 34 without sections. Here they are grouped by marks:
Section A: questions 1 to 20 (1 mark each)
Section B: questions 21 to 24 (3 marks each)
Section C: questions 25 to 30 (4 marks each)
Section D: questions 31 to 34 (6 marks each)
Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
This is a practice paper written in the pattern of the CBSE Sample Question Paper 2026-27. It is not an official CBSE paper.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Prakash Industries completed its production target of 10,000 units on time. However, it used much more raw material and labour than was necessary, which pushed up its costs. Which of the following describes the management of Prakash Industries?
questions.sol: Effectiveness means completing the job on time (achieving the target). Efficiency means doing it with the minimum cost and least wastage of resources. The target was met on time, but resources were wasted, so the management was effective but not efficient.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: The management of Arya Motors invites suggestions from workers on how to cut costs and improve methods, and gives cash rewards for every suggestion that is put into use. Which principle of Scientific Management is being followed?
options: Development of each and every person to his or her greatest efficiency and prosperity
questions.sol: Under 'cooperation, not individualism', management should not close its ears to constructive suggestions made by employees, and employees should be rewarded for suggestions that result in substantial reduction in costs.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Sona Paper Mills is a large company that makes only one product, writing paper. Its work needs a high degree of specialisation in production, finance, marketing and human resources. Which organisation structure is most suitable for it?
questions.sol: A functional structure groups jobs by major functions such as production, finance and marketing. It is most suitable when the organisation is large, has a single or a few product lines and needs a high degree of specialisation. A divisional structure suits a company with several distinct product lines.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Read the following statements carefully:
Statement I: Recruitment is a negative process, as it rejects unsuitable candidates.
Statement II: Selection is a negative process, as it involves the rejection of unsuitable candidates.
Choose the correct option from the following:
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statement II is true and Statement I is false.
questions.sol: Recruitment is a positive process: it encourages as many people as possible to apply for the job. Selection is a negative process, because it involves the rejection of unsuitable candidates. So Statement I is false and Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A new law made it compulsory for manufacturers to print a statutory health warning on every packet of tobacco products. Identify the dimension of business environment involved.
questions.sol: The legal environment includes legislation passed by Parliament and other legal requirements that a business must follow. A statutory warning required by law is a part of the legal environment.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes a free-rein (laissez faire) leader?
options: The leader gives followers a high degree of independence to set their own objectives and only supports them with the information they need.
The leader gives orders and expects them to be obeyed, so communication is one-way.
The leader develops plans and takes decisions in consultation with the followers.
The leader depends mainly on rewards and punishments to get the work done.
questions.sol: A laissez faire or free-rein leader does not use power unless it is absolutely essential. Followers are given a high degree of independence, and the leader is there only to support them and supply the required information. The other options describe autocratic and democratic leaders.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following statements about the primary market is correct?
options: Securities that have already been issued are bought and sold among investors.
It has a fixed geographical location where trading takes place.
Prices of securities are determined by the demand and supply on the stock exchange.
It deals with new securities and directly promotes capital formation.
questions.sol: The primary (new issues) market deals with new securities issued for the first time, so funds flow directly from investors to the company and capital formation is promoted directly. The other statements describe the secondary market.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Ravi is not satisfied with the order passed by the District Commission on his complaint against a mobile phone company. Where can he file an appeal against this order?
questions.sol: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, an appeal against an order of the District Commission can be made to the State Commission.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: The manager of a call centre always says 'we' instead of 'I' when she talks to her team. She gives the team credit for its success and encourages its members to work together in harmony. Which principle of management does she follow?
questions.sol: Esprit de corps means that management should promote team spirit, unity and harmony among employees. Fayol suggested that a manager should replace 'I' with 'we' in all conversations to foster team spirit.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Consumer protection is important for consumers as well as for businesses.
Reason (R): Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a complaint can be filed only by the consumer who bought the goods.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.sol: A is true: consumer protection safeguards consumers and is also in the long-term interest of business, as satisfied customers bring repeat sales, and it is part of the social responsibility of business. R is false: besides the consumer, a registered consumers' association, the Central or a State Government, one or more consumers having the same interest, and the legal heir or representative of a deceased consumer can also file a complaint.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is a function of consumer organisations and NGOs in India?
options: Fixing the prices of essential goods
Passing orders for the refund of the price paid by consumers
Granting quality certification marks to products
Educating the general public about consumer rights by organising training programmes and seminars
questions.sol: Consumer organisations and NGOs educate the general public about consumer rights through training programmes, seminars and workshops. Passing refund orders is done by the consumer commissions; price fixing and quality certification are not their functions.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Kavi Foods Ltd., a biscuit manufacturer, has decided to start making chocolates and soft drinks as well. This will need new plant and machinery. Identify the factor affecting its fixed capital requirement.
questions.sol: A firm may choose to diversify its operations for various reasons. With diversification into new product lines, the requirement of fixed capital rises, since new plant and machinery are needed.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Name the two depositories in India that hold securities in electronic form.
questions.sol: The two depositories in India are the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL) and the Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL). BSE and NSE are stock exchanges, and SEBI and RBI are regulators.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: After fixing the target of opening 20 new stores in a year, the managers of Supermart made assumptions about the future: that consumer spending would rise, shop rents would remain stable and no new competitor would enter the region. Identify the step of the planning process described.
questions.sol: Developing premises means making assumptions about the future, which form the base on which plans are drawn. Here the objective had already been set; the managers then made assumptions about spending, rents and competition.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: The Finance Manager of Orbit Ltd. accepts only those proposals that are expected to increase the market price of the company's equity shares. Which objective of financial management does this reflect?
options: Maximising the sales of the company
Minimising the tax paid by the company
Maximising the wealth of the shareholders
questions.sol: The primary objective of financial management is to maximise shareholders' wealth, which is reflected in the market price of the equity shares. Decisions that increase the market price of shares serve this objective.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A car manufacturer sells its cars to consumers through authorised dealers (retailers) in each city. Identify the channel of distribution used.
questions.sol: In a one level channel there is one middleman, the retailer, between the manufacturer and the consumer: manufacturer → retailer → consumer.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Sagar Shipyard takes about two years to build one ship. During this period large amounts of money remain locked up in raw materials and partly built ships. Identify the factor that makes its working capital requirement high.
questions.sol: The production cycle is the time span between the receipt of raw material and its conversion into finished goods. The longer the production cycle, the larger the working capital required.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: To build its image as a responsible company, Fitwell Ltd. sponsored a city marathon, organised a free health camp and issued press releases about these events. Identify the element of the promotion mix used.
questions.sol: Public relations aims at building a good image and goodwill for the company among the public, through activities such as sponsoring events, community programmes and press releases.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: A company has earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of ₹12,00,000. It has issued ₹30,00,000 of 10% debentures. What is its interest coverage ratio?
questions.sol: Interest = 10% of ₹30,00,000 = ₹3,00,000. Interest coverage ratio = EBIT ÷ interest = ₹12,00,000 ÷ ₹3,00,000 = 4 times.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: In Speedo Motors Ltd., the management keeps a close and constant watch on the cost of steel, the quality of engines and the safety of workers, because even a small deviation in any of these key areas can affect the success of the whole organisation. Identify the concept of controlling followed.
questions.sol: Critical point control means that control should focus on the key result areas (KRAs), which are critical to the success of the organisation, because a small change in them affects the whole organisation.

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: State the last three steps in the process of selection of employees.
questions.model:
1. Medical examination: After the selection decision and before the job offer is made, the candidate is required to undergo a medical fitness test.
2. Job offer: The candidate who has cleared all the earlier steps is offered the job through a letter of appointment. The letter generally contains the date by which the appointee must report on duty, and the candidate is given reasonable time to accept the offer.
3. Contract of employment: After the job offer is accepted, the employer and the candidate sign documents such as the contract of employment, which gives details such as job title, duties, date of joining, pay and allowances, hours of work and leave rules.

points.t: Medical examination, with a brief statement of what it involves
Job offer, with a brief statement of what it involves
Contract of employment, with a brief statement of what it involves

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Ramesh, the Operations Manager of a courier company, sent a long email full of technical terms to the delivery staff about a new parcel-tracking system. Many of the staff did not understand it, and Ramesh never checked whether they had. The next week, many deliveries were recorded wrongly.
State any three measures Ramesh should adopt to make his communication effective.
questions.model:
Measures to improve the effectiveness of communication (any three):
1. Communicate according to the needs of the receiver: the message should be adjusted to the level of understanding of the receiver (here, the delivery staff).
2. Be aware of language, tone and content: the language should be simple and understandable, without technical jargon.
3. Ensure proper feedback: the communicator may ask questions to check whether the message has been understood, and encourage the receivers to respond.
4. Clarify the ideas before communication: the problem or idea should be clear in the communicator's own mind before it is passed on.
5. Follow up communications: the manager should regularly review the instructions given and remove any hurdles in implementing them.

points.t: First measure correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Second measure correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Third measure correctly stated (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: State any three points of importance of financial planning.
questions.model:
Importance of financial planning (any three):
1. It tries to forecast what may happen in future under different business situations, so the firm is better prepared to face the future.
2. It helps in avoiding business shocks and surprises, and helps the company prepare for the future.
3. It helps in coordinating various business functions, such as sales and production, by providing clear policies and procedures.
4. Detailed plans of action prepared under financial planning reduce waste, duplication of efforts and gaps in planning.
5. It tries to link the present with the future.
6. It provides a link between investment and financing decisions on a continuous basis.
7. By spelling out detailed objectives for the various business segments, it makes the evaluation of actual performance easier.

points.t: First point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Second point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Third point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: State any three points of importance of controlling.
questions.model:
Importance of controlling (any three):
1. Accomplishing organisational goals: controlling measures progress towards the goals and brings to light deviations, if any, so that corrective action can be taken.
2. Judging accuracy of standards: a good control system enables management to verify whether the standards set are accurate and objective.
3. Making efficient use of resources: by exercising control, a manager seeks to reduce wastage and spoilage of resources.
4. Improving employee motivation: employees know well in advance what they are expected to do and the standards on which they will be appraised.
5. Ensuring order and discipline: close checks on the activities of employees create an atmosphere of order and discipline and reduce dishonest behaviour.
6. Facilitating coordination in action: each department and employee is governed by predetermined standards that are well coordinated with one another.

points.t: First point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Second point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Third point correctly stated (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Excel Tools Ltd. found that a single foreman could not be an expert in every aspect of the work. It therefore separated planning from execution and placed several specialists over the workers. Under the production incharge, one specialist ensures that each job is completed on time, another keeps machines, tools and materials ready for the workers, a third keeps the machines in proper working condition, and a fourth checks the quality of the work.

parts.q: (a) Name the technique of Scientific Management adopted by Excel Tools Ltd.

points.t: Functional foremanship

parts.q: (b) Name any three of the four specialists working under the production incharge described above, and state the role of each.
parts.model:
Specialists under the production incharge (any three):
1. Speed boss: ensures the timely and accurate completion of jobs.
2. Gang boss: keeps machines, tools and materials ready for operation by the workers.
3. Repair boss: ensures that the machines are kept in proper working condition.
4. Inspector: checks the quality of the work.

points.t: First specialist correctly named (any one from the model answer)
First specialist: role correctly stated
Second specialist correctly named
Second specialist: role correctly stated
Third specialist correctly named
Third specialist: role correctly stated

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Glorious Textiles has grown from 50 employees to over 2,000 employees in ten years. It now has separate departments for purchase, production, finance and marketing, and each department wants to pursue its own targets. The company has also hired many specialists, who often think that only they know what is best for the company. As a result, the efforts of different people and departments are no longer moving in the same direction.

parts.q: (a) Name the concept of management that the company needs to bring the efforts of all these people and departments together.
parts.model: Coordination: the process by which a manager synchronises the activities of different departments and individuals towards the common goals of the organisation.

points.t: Coordination

parts.q: (b) Explain the three reasons, highlighted in the case, why this concept is needed.
parts.model:
1. Growth in size: As an organisation grows in size, the number of people employed also increases. Each individual has his or her own needs and goals, so coordination is needed to integrate individual goals with organisational goals ('grown from 50 employees to over 2,000 employees').
2. Functional differentiation: An organisation is divided into departments such as purchase, production, finance and marketing, each of which may pursue its own objectives. Coordination is needed to link their activities ('each department wants to pursue its own targets').
3. Specialisation: Specialists usually feel that they are qualified to judge matters according to their own views, which may cause conflict. Coordination is needed to reconcile their differences ('specialists, who often think that only they know what is best').

points.t: Growth in size, identified
Growth in size, explained
Functional differentiation, identified
Functional differentiation, explained
Specialisation, identified
Specialisation, explained

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Demonetisation is an example of how a single decision of the government can change the business environment for every business in the country. Answer the following questions about it.

parts.model: Demonetisation means withdrawing the status of legal tender from a currency. On November 8, 2016, the Government of India announced that the two largest denomination notes, ₹500 and ₹1000, would cease to be legal tender from midnight.

points.t: Meaning: notes cease to be legal tender (the ₹500 and ₹1000 notes, announced on 8 November 2016)

parts.q: (b) State any three features of demonetisation.
parts.model:
Features of demonetisation (any three):
1. It is viewed as a tax administration measure: cash from declared income was deposited in banks, while those with black money had to declare their unaccounted wealth and pay tax at a penalty rate.
2. It was interpreted as a sign from the government that tax evasion would no longer be tolerated or accepted.
3. It led to the channelising of savings into the formal financial system, as cash was deposited in banks.
4. It aimed at creating a less-cash or cash-lite economy, encouraging digital transactions.

points.t: First feature correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Second feature correctly stated (any one from the model answer)
Third feature correctly stated (any one from the model answer)

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Navya Software Ltd. uses the following measures to motivate its employees:
(i) Employees receive a share in the profits of the company every year.
(ii) Employees are offered shares of the company at a price lower than the market price.
(iii) Employees are provided with a car and a house rent allowance over and above their salary.
(iv) Employees receive provident fund, pension and gratuity after they retire.
Identify the financial incentive used in each of these measures.
questions.model:
(i) Profit sharing: employees are given a share in the profits of the organisation, which motivates them to improve their performance.
(ii) Co-partnership or employee stock option: employees are offered company shares at a set price lower than the market price, which gives them a feeling of ownership.
(iii) Perquisites: fringe benefits such as car allowance, housing, medical aid and education for children, over and above the salary.
(iv) Retirement benefits: benefits such as provident fund, pension and gratuity, which give financial security after retirement.

points.t: (i) Profit sharing
(ii) Co-partnership / employee stock option
(iii) Perquisites (fringe benefits)
(iv) Retirement benefits

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: 'Planning and controlling are inseparable twins of management.' Explain this statement with the help of any four points.
questions.model:
Relationship between planning and controlling (any four):
1. Planning is the basis of controlling: planning provides the goals or standards against which actual performance is measured. Without planning there is nothing to control; controlling is blind without planning.
2. Controlling makes planning effective: controlling checks whether the plans are being achieved and brings to light the deviations, so that corrective action can be taken. Planning without controlling is meaningless.
3. Planning is prescriptive, while controlling is evaluative: planning lays down what should be done, while controlling evaluates whether decisions have been translated into the desired action.
4. Planning is looking ahead and controlling is looking back, but this is only partly true: planning is also guided by past experience, and the corrective action taken under controlling aims to improve future performance. So both look ahead as well as back.
5. Planning and controlling reinforce each other: planning based on facts makes controlling easier and more effective, and controlling improves future planning by providing information from past experience.

points.t: First point: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
First point: correct explanation of that heading
Second point: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Second point: correct explanation of that heading
Third point: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Third point: correct explanation of that heading
Fourth point: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Fourth point: correct explanation of that heading

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text: Explain any four advantages of branding to marketers.
questions.model:
Advantages of branding to marketers (any four):
1. Enables marketers to distinguish their product from those of competitors: it becomes possible to secure and control the market for the product, because a branded product can be easily identified.
2. Helps in creating product image and advertising: without a brand name, a firm cannot advertise its product well. With a brand name, advertising and display programmes become effective.
3. Enables the firm to charge a different price: a brand becomes a symbol of status and quality, so the firm can charge a price different from that of its competitors.
4. Ease in introduction of new products: if a new product is introduced under an existing, well-known brand name, it is easier to introduce and sell it.

points.t: First advantage: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
First advantage: correct explanation of that heading
Second advantage: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Second advantage: correct explanation of that heading
Third advantage: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Third advantage: correct explanation of that heading
Fourth advantage: correct heading (any one from the model answer)
Fourth advantage: correct explanation of that heading

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Explain the following types of plans:
(a) Objective
(b) Policy
(c) Budget
questions.model:
(a) Objective: Objectives are the end results which management seeks to achieve through its operations. They represent the desired future position of the organisation. Objectives are usually set by top management, should be expressed in specific terms and be measurable in quantitative terms, for example 'to increase sales by 10% this year'.
(b) Policy: Policies are general statements that guide thinking or channelise energies towards a particular direction. They provide a basis for interpreting strategy and are guides to managerial action and decisions, for example the recruitment policy or the pricing policy of a firm.
(c) Budget: A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms for a definite future period, for example a sales budget giving the expected sales of each product in each area for the next year. It is also a control device, as actual performance can be compared with the budgeted figures.

points.t: (a) Objective: end results that management seeks to achieve
(a) Objective: expressed in specific, measurable terms (with or without an example)
(b) Policy: general statements that guide thinking and decision making
(b) Policy: basis for interpreting strategy, with an example such as a recruitment or pricing policy
(c) Budget: statement of expected results in numerical terms for a definite period
(c) Budget: also a control device / suitable example such as a sales budget

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Mehta Events Pvt. Ltd. won a contract to organise a three-day book fair. The manager first listed all the work to be done, such as booking the venue, inviting publishers, publicity, ticketing and security, and broke it into manageable tasks. Similar tasks were then grouped together into units such as Venue, Publicity and Ticketing. Each unit was handed over to staff members who had the right skills and experience for that work. Finally, the manager made it clear who would report to whom, so that everyone knew from whom to take orders and to whom to report.
Identify and explain the four steps in the process of organising discussed above.
questions.model:
1. Identification and division of work: The total work to be done is identified and divided into manageable activities, so that duplication of effort is avoided and the burden of work is shared ('listed all the work ... broke it into manageable tasks').
2. Departmentalisation: Activities of a similar nature are grouped together into departments or units, which facilitates specialisation ('grouped together into units such as Venue, Publicity and Ticketing').
3. Assignment of duties: Work is allocated to people according to their skills and competence, so that each job is done by the person best suited to it ('handed over to staff members who had the right skills').
4. Establishing reporting relationships: Each individual is told from whom to take orders and to whom he or she is accountable. This creates a hierarchical structure and helps in coordination ('who would report to whom').

points.t: Identification and division of work, identified
Identification and division of work, explained
Departmentalisation, identified
Departmentalisation, explained
Assignment of duties, identified
Assignment of duties, explained
Establishing reporting relationships, identified
Establishing reporting relationships, explained

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Distinguish between capital market and money market on the basis of:
(a) Participants (b) Investment outlay (c) Duration (d) Liquidity (e) Safety (f) Expected return
questions.model:
BasisCapital marketMoney market
(a) ParticipantsFinancial institutions, banks, corporate entities, foreign investors and ordinary retail investors from the public.Largely institutions such as banks, financial institutions, the RBI and the government.
(b) Investment outlayDoes not need a huge outlay, as the value of units of securities is generally low (such as ₹10 or ₹100 per share).Transactions involve huge sums of money, as the instruments are quite expensive.
(c) DurationDeals in medium-term and long-term securities.Deals in short-term instruments with a maximum maturity of one year.
(d) LiquiditySecurities are liquid, as they are marketable on stock exchanges.Instruments have a higher degree of liquidity, as there is a formal arrangement for it.
(e) SafetyRiskier, both with respect to returns and repayment of principal.Much safer, with a minimum risk of default, because of the short duration and the financial soundness of the issuers.
(f) Expected returnHigher, because of the chance of dividends and capital gains over a longer period.Lower.

points.t: (a) Participants correctly distinguished
(b) Investment outlay correctly distinguished
(c) Duration correctly distinguished
(d) Liquidity correctly distinguished
(e) Safety correctly distinguished
(f) Expected return correctly distinguished

questions.subject: Business Studies
questions.text:
Explain the following marketing philosophies:
(a) Product concept
(b) Selling concept
(c) Marketing concept
questions.model:
(a) Product concept: It holds that customers prefer products of good quality, performance and features, and are ready to pay a higher price for them. The focus of business is on product improvement, i.e., improving the quality and features of the product, and profit is earned through product quality.
(b) Selling concept: It holds that customers will not buy enough of the firm's products unless they are persuaded to buy them. The focus is on selling the existing products through aggressive selling and promotion efforts, and profit is earned through a large volume of sales.
(c) Marketing concept: It holds that the key to success lies in identifying the needs and wants of the target market and satisfying them better than competitors. The focus is on customer needs, the means used is integrated marketing, and profit is earned through customer satisfaction.

points.t: (a) Product concept: customers prefer products of good quality, performance and features
(a) Product concept: focus on product improvement; profit through product quality
(b) Selling concept: customers buy only when persuaded
(b) Selling concept: focus on selling and promotion; profit through sales volume
(c) Marketing concept: identifying and satisfying customer needs better than competitors
(c) Marketing concept: integrated marketing as the means; profit through customer satisfaction
